what is pascals triangle and why is it famous

Start with a single 1. why is the international date line not a straight line

It mostly follows the 180 degree meridian, the line opposite Greenwich, where one calendar date hands over to the next. 🌏 But it swerves around Kiribati, Samoa and Russia's far east so that no country ends up split across two dates. Time boundaries are agreements, not geometry, and countries do move them when trade or daily life demands it.

why does electricity travel on those huge towers instead of ordinary wires

Wires waste power as heat, and the waste grows with the current, not the voltage. So the grid trades one for the other: transformers push the voltage very high, the same power then travels as a far smaller current, and much less is lost over hundreds of kilometres. Transformers near your street bring it back down. 🗼 Those lines stay deadly, which is why they hang out of reach. [CHIPS]How do transformers work?|What is voltage?[/CHIPS]

how do hospitals decide who gets seen first in casualty

Not by arrival time — by triage. A nurse assesses everyone quickly on one question: how fast could this person get worse? So someone sitting quietly but struggling to breathe goes ahead of someone in loud pain from a broken finger, which feels unfair from the waiting room and is the reason emergency departments save the people they do. If anything changes while you wait, tell the triage nurse. 🏥[FACT]Triage comes from a French word meaning to sort.[/FACT][CHIPS]What does triage mean?|Who assesses first?|Why the long wait?[/CHIPS]

whats the difference between a bug and a feature

A bug is a gap between what the code does and what it was meant to do. Which means every bug argument secretly needs a spec: without agreement on meant to, you are debating intent, not code. 🐛 That is the whole joke in it is not a bug, it is a feature — someone quietly redefined meant to. Writing the expected behaviour down first is how real teams end that argument. [CHIPS]What is a spec|Try writing one|A real example[/CHIPS]

why do i feel heavy when the lift starts going up

Because for a second you genuinely are heavier, as far as the floor is concerned. To get you moving upwards the floor must push harder than your weight, and that extra push is what your legs feel. Once the lift settles into a steady speed the feeling vanishes, which is the giveaway: your body notices acceleration, not motion. 🛗 Ride one and notice where the feeling starts and stops.

why do tamil sentences put the verb at the end

Because Tamil is a subject-object-verb language, and that is simply where its verb lives. 📚 "Naan paal kudichen" is literally "I milk drank". English settled on subject-verb-object instead, but neither order is more logical — Japanese, Korean and Turkish all park the verb at the end too, and none of them is related to Tamil. Word order is a habit a language settles into, not a sign of how it thinks.

why do french nouns have genders when tamil nouns do not

Grammatical gender is mostly inherited accident, not logic — la table is feminine for no reason a table would recognise. Languages keep these classes because agreement rules get baked into adjectives, articles and verbs, so ripping them out would break everything at once. Tamil sorts nouns on a different axis, roughly rational versus non-rational, which is its own class system 🇫🇷.

how does a footballer bend a free kick around the wall

Strike across the ball with the inside of the foot and you leave it spinning sideways as it flies. A spinning ball drags air faster round one side than the other, so the pressure difference nudges it off a straight line — physicists call it the Magnus effect. ⚽ The curve grows as the ball slows near the end, which is why the bend looks so sudden. Same physics as a table-tennis topspin dip.

why do the monsoon winds change direction twice a year

what is reverse swing and why does it need an old ball

whats the polite way to say you in tamil

Tamil splits "you" much the way French does. 🙏 Nee is for close friends, siblings and people younger than you. Neenga is the respectful form — elders, teachers, shopkeepers, anyone you have just met — and it doubles as the plural. So "eppadi irukkeenga?" is the polite "how are you?", while "eppadi irukka?" is what you would say to a classmate. Default to neenga with adults; nobody is ever offended by extra respect.

why do people sprinkle salt on icy roads

Salt lowers the temperature at which water freezes. Dissolved salt particles keep getting in the way of water molecules trying to lock into an ice crystal, so the ice needs to be colder than usual to hold together — and at ordinary winter temperatures it melts instead. In a deep enough freeze, though, plain salt stops helping. ❄️

how small can a microscope actually see

Light itself sets the limit. 🔬 A wave cannot resolve anything much smaller than about half its own wavelength, so an ordinary light microscope stops near 200 nanometres — fine for cells and bacteria, useless for a virus. why can't i see colours properly in a dark room

Your retina carries two kinds of sensor. Cones read colour but need a decent amount of light; rods are far more sensitive yet report no colour at all. In dim light only the rods have enough signal to speak, so the room arrives in shades of grey. Nothing is wrong with your eyes — the colour system has simply run out of light. 👁️ [FACT]Eyes take about half an hour to fully adapt to darkness.[/FACT][CHIPS]Why use red light?|How long to adjust?[/CHIPS]

why is tamil so different from hindi

Hindi belongs to a completely different family, Indo-European, which also holds Persian, Greek and English; inside that family Hindi sits on the Indo-Aryan branch. Centuries of living side by side means the two swap words freely — but the skeleton underneath is built differently.

why do i feel dizzy when i stand up too fast

why does my air dry clay shrink and warp as it dries

Air dry clay is solid particles floating in water, so every drop that leaves lets the particles pull closer and the piece has to get smaller 🏺. Slow it down with a loose bag, even walls and no direct sun.

Every dinosaur roar you have ever heard was built by a sound engineer out of living animals. 🦕 Voice boxes are soft tissue and almost never fossilise, so nobody has the real sound and nobody ever will. is it true that most indian scripts are cousins of each other

Yes, and the family resemblance is structural, not just visual. Tamil, Devanagari, Telugu, Bengali and several South-East Asian scripts all descend from Brahmi, in use in India over two thousand years ago. why do websites not store your actual password

Because a stolen database should not hand over your login. Sites store a hash instead: a one-way scramble that is easy to run forwards and impractical to run backwards. When you sign in they hash what you typed and compare scrambles, never the password itself — which is why a real site can reset your password but can never tell you the old one. 🔐 Good sites pick a deliberately slow hash too, so guessing millions of passwords stays expensive. [CHIPS]What is a hash|Why salting helps|Spot a bad site[/CHIPS]
